verdicts.reason: A has a clear centered stack (logo > big headline > subhead), but the CTA is shrunk to a tiny pill and jammed against a block of illegibly small legal copy on the same row, and the suitcase is cropped against the top edge. B scatters the elements: the logo floats alone at the left middle, the tiny CTA pill sits next to the headline, the subhead is offset under it, and the legal text runs across the full width at the bottom, so the reading order is jumbled. Both are weak; A is less bad because its hierarchy and grouping read more clearly.
